tasks.title: Experimental `avera check --json` v0 evidence envelope (issue #12)
tasks.description: Add an additive, digest-bound evidence envelope (`avera.check/v0`) to `avera check --json` so downstream review tools (first consumer: CounterProof) can attach an AVERA result as external evidence. Shape agreed in mikheil-galoian/avera#12 and hippoley/CounterProof#81.
tasks.details: Envelope keys: schema_version='avera.check/v0', tool{name,version}, policy, inputs{baseline_sha256,current_sha256} (SHA-256 of the JUnit file bytes), result{verdict,gate_status,introduced_failures,risk,confidence,confidence_score}, digest. Digest rule (explicit, per reviewer): SHA-256 lowercase hex over UTF-8 JSON with recursively sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace, `digest` excluded. Boundaries: v0/unstable; digest = change detection, not authenticity; AVERA verdict spec stays authoritative; input hashes identify the JUnit artifacts, NOT the source candidates that produced them; no CounterProof-specific field; existing --json keys unchanged (additive `evidence` key). Also fixes __version__ (0.1.0) drifting from pyproject (0.1.1), since the envelope reports it.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests for digest determinism, exclusion of `digest`, tamper detection, input hashing; CLI test that --json keeps old keys and adds a verifiable `evidence`; golden test that rebuilds the frozen example envelope byte-for-byte; version guard test (__version__ == pyproject). Full pytest, fixture matrix, ruff, build green.

subtasks.title: Wire `evidence` into `avera check --json` (additive) with CLI test

Full verification, PR, reply on CounterProof#81 with example link

tasks.title: v0 numeric conformance vectors + producer guard (CounterProof #168 finding)
tasks.description: A second-language (Node) verifier showed Python and JS format some numbers differently (1.0 vs 1, -0.0 vs 0, 1e-07 vs 1e-7), so the v0 digest is not cross-language for those values. Keep v0 unchanged (agreed: documented boundary, not a protocol defect); make the boundary explicit and guard the producer.
tasks.details: Spec: add numeric conformance vectors (value, Python canonical form, digest of the frozen example with that score) and state the current producer property: confidence_score has 2 decimals, never integral. Test: enumerate every branch of _confidence_factors x all verdicts x all labels; assert 0 < score < 1 and 2-decimal (so it formats identically in Python and JS). Fails if a cap becomes 1.0 or enough negative factors are added to reach 0.0.
tasks.testStrategy: New guard test passes now; temporarily setting a cap to 1.0 or adding negative factors makes it fail. Vectors in spec are computed by the reference implementation and checked by a test. Full pytest green.

tasks.title: EP-09: Change coverage mapping
tasks.description: Turn (diff, coverage report) into one deterministic number: what fraction of the changed lines in a change is covered by any test. Zero new dependencies (stdlib text/XML parsing only). Design doc: docs/AVERA_CHANGE_IMPACT_STAGE.md.
tasks.details: Parses unified diff -> per-file changed line ranges (added/modified only; deleted lines carry nothing to cover). Parses LCOV (lcov.info) and Cobertura XML into per-file executed-line sets, covering the common output of pytest-cov, Jest/Istanbul, JaCoCo, coverage.py, grcov, Go. Computes coverage_of_change per file and aggregate, with the uncovered-line list as first-class output. Fails closed: a diffed file absent from the coverage report counts as fully uncovered, never skipped.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests per parser (diff, LCOV, Cobertura) against hand-built fixtures and at least one real tool's real output each. Determinism test (same inputs -> same output). Fail-closed test: file in diff, absent from coverage report, is reported uncovered. Full pytest green.

subtasks.title: US-09.1: unified diff -> per-file changed line ranges
US-09.2: LCOV parser -> per-file executed-line sets
US-09.3: Cobertura XML parser -> per-file executed-line sets
US-09.4: coverage_of_change computation, fail-closed on missing files

tasks.title: EP-10: Change-targeted mutation
tasks.description: Upgrade 'covered' to 'verified' automatically: run the existing mutation lens (T-13's run_mutation_lens) on changed+covered regions from EP-09, bounded by a budget. Depends on task 9.
tasks.details: Extends run_mutation_lens to accept an explicit (start_line, end_line) range additive to the current function= parameter (the engine already supports line-range mutation internally via generate_mutants). For each changed+covered region, runs the lens under a max-mutants/max-seconds budget; over-budget regions are marked 'not evaluated' explicitly, never silently reported as weak or strong. Combines into one verdict: uncovered lines, weak-evidence lines (covered but mutation score below threshold), aggregate score.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test for the new line-range entry point (equivalent to the existing function= path on the same input). Budget test: a region that exceeds the budget is marked not-evaluated, distinct from evaluated-and-weak. Full pytest green; mutation lens dogfooded on the new module per existing project convention.

subtasks.title: US-10.1: run_mutation_lens accepts an explicit line range
US-10.2: automatic budgeted mutation over changed+covered regions
US-10.3: combined verdict (uncovered / weak-evidence / aggregate score)
